name: Tripod 5-axis CoreXY 0.4 nozzle
printer_notes: Research design, docs/nonplanar/kinematics/tripod: a Voron Trident 250 whose toolhead is a 3-PRS tripod wrist (three NEMA 11 linear steppers on MGN12 rails at 45 mm, 110 mm blade struts, platform 30 mm, Revo Six 50 mm under the ball plane). The wrist reaches a 60 deg cone toward every azimuth. The slicer drives it as head_ab with the pivot 50 mm up the tool (rotary_tool_length), A and B within the cone; the tripod's own IK (kinematics/kin.py) turns A, B and the tip height into the three slider positions, and its common mode is a 90 mm/s local Z (machine_max_speed_z). rotary_max_speed is the tilt rate at the upright pose (191 deg/s at 100 mm/s per slider); slower poses (79 deg/s at the edge of the cone) are corrected in joint space (slicer/RESULTS.md). XY speeds are the Prodcan3's so the rotary-suite ratios compare kinematics, not motors. Not built; calibrated=false.
